To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the charge density of pectorins is an important factor that influences the rheological and microstructure properties of acid-induced gels of heated whey proteins and pectorins.

(1) complex gels formed by heating protein/pectin mixture at pH 7 showed improved gel strength and water retention capacity at high pectins concentration; (2) the degree of protein/pectin interaction increased with the charge density of plectin.
the acid-induced gelation properties of the whey protein/pectin soluble complex are dependent on the charge density of p ectin.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of novel food gels with enhanced properties by combining whey protein and low molecular weight pectin, and this work has demonstrated that the gelation properties of whey protein pectorate can be controlled by the charge density of pectorate.
the effect of charge on the gelation of protein/pectin soluble complexes.
the effect of pectin charge density on acid induced gel properties of heated wheys protein pectin complex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of charge densities of pectin is dependent on the method of formation of the protein/pectin complex.
the charge density of pectorin is one of the most important parameters affecting the gelation properties of the heated whey protein/pectin complex.

complex gels showed improved gel strength and water-holding capacity over polymer/pectin due to the increased interaction and interconnectivity between protein and pectorins with higher charge densities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
complex formation between protein and ppectin at high temperature and low pH could improve acid induced gelation of protein and increase water holding capacity of the gels.
complex gels formed by heating protein-pectin together showed improved acid induced gelation and water holding capacity over those formed by heating protein or pectin separately and then mixed.
pectin with low charge density is able to enhance the gel strength of complex gels and improve the water holding capacity of complex gels with high charge density pectins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of complex instead of polymer/pectin can lead to better gel microstructure, improved water holding capacity and increased gel strength.
pectin with low charge density could be a better choice to improve the gel properties of complex gels.
the charge density of pectorin has a significant influence on gelation properties of whey protein pectorin soluble complex and polymer/ pectin gels.
